answer.rationale: Promotional pricing is explicitly ruled out by exp_73 data: acquired cohort fails at renewal, and the competitor's move creates urgency that would push us toward the same trap. Defensive discounting does not maximize sustainable qualified revenue—it erodes it. Instead, activate three proven levers in concert: (1) referral incentives (memory_57) convert existing satisfied customers into repeatable acquisition channels without retention harm; (2) shortened onboarding (memory_86, exp_86) accelerates time-to-value and retention for any new cohort; (3) in-product activation messaging (memory_91) ensures new accounts reach first meaningful action. This bundle addresses churn risk by retaining *quality* customers and shifting acquisition toward advocates rather than price-driven, low-tenure accounts. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is secondary—it requires longer sales cycles we don't have time for today. Referral + onboarding + activation messaging can deploy within days, protecting the base while building sustainable growth. Scale as standard experiment to measure cohort durability before full rollout, preserving signal and option value.
